							25 text entry area (settable) Apa yang ingin dibuat? Create a high-quality, fully textured 3D model of a fierce shark matching the provided reference image. The reference shows multiple camera views of ONE shark. Generate only one complete shark model.  SUBJECT AND SHAPE A powerful, intimidating great white shark with a muscular, streamlined body. Broad head, pointed snout, thick torso, and a tapered tail section. Maintain a recognizable shark silhouette with realistic aquatic anatomy and slightly exaggerated strength.  The shark must look aggressive from every angle. Use small, deeply set eyes, a pronounced brow, and an open mouth showing multiple rows of sharp triangular teeth. Keep the jaw opening anatomically believable and integrate it naturally with the head.  ANATOMY Include one large triangular dorsal fin, a smaller second dorsal fin, two pectoral fins, two pelvic fins, a small anal fin, and a strong asymmetrical crescent-shaped tail with a longer upper lobe.  Include five distinct gill slits on each side behind the head. Connect every fin smoothly to the body. Keep the left and right sides anatomically consistent.  COLOR AND MARKINGS Use dark charcoal and graphite gray across the upper body, transitioning to a pale gray underside.  Add vivid crimson-red markings along both flanks. The markings should form irregular, streamlined streaks that follow the body's shape from behind the gills toward the tail.  Add crimson accents to the dorsal fin, pectoral fin tips, and tail edges. These red areas are natural skin pigmentation, not blood, wounds, armor, or separate objects.  Eyes should have deep red irises and dark pupils. Teeth should be ivory white with slightly darker roots. Use dark, desaturated flesh tones inside the mouth.  SURFACE AND MATERIALS Create realistic, finely detailed shark skin with subtle microtexture. The surface should have a slightly wet satin appearance, with controlled highlights and varied roughness.  Use physically based materials. Skin must be non-metallic. Preserve readable surface detail without making the body look rocky, heavily wrinkled, or covered in scales.  Keep the red markings integrated into the skin material. Avoid strong emissive effects. Do not bake dramatic lighting or cast shadows into the base color texture.  MOUTH AND TEETH Model the open mouth with visible depth, a clean gum line, and a coherent inner mouth cavity. Teeth must be individually readable, firmly attached, and arranged in organized rows.  Avoid intersecting teeth, floating teeth, distorted jaws, or holes through the head. The mouth should remain convincing from front, side, and low-angle views.  POSE Use a neutral swimming pose suitable for inspection and future rigging. Keep the body approximately straight, the tail aligned with the body, and the pectoral fins naturally extended.  Do not use an extreme turning pose or strongly curved spine. Preserve the aggressive expression through the head shape, eyes, and open jaw.  MODEL QUALITY Create a complete 360-degree model, including the back, underside, fins, tail, and mouth interior.  Use clean geometry, coherent edge flow, and sufficient detail around the face, gills, fin roots, and mouth. Keep fin edges thin but give them real thickness. Avoid accidental holes, self-intersections, disconnected parts, and overlapping surfaces.  Use clean UV mapping with consistent texture density and minimal visible seams. If supported, provide PBR base color, roughness, normal, and ambient occlusion maps.  OUTPUT One isolated shark asset, centered at the origin, with its length aligned along a primary horizontal axis. No environment, water, floor, pedestal, props, text, or additional creatures.  Prioritize the reference shark's silhouette, charcoal-and-crimson palette, fierce expression, and consistent appearance from every camera angle.  REBUILD FOR REFERENCE FIDELITY — LOCAL FORGEKIT / OBSIDIAN / BLENDER ONLY The earlier model was visually wrong. Build a fresh, much more faithful model from the attached six-view shark reference. Do not preserve its capsule-shaped head, circular tube mouth, straight triangular fins, or floating red plates. Use the connected Obsidian model-3d guides.  The trusted mesh primitive now supports subdivision: 1 or 2. Use anatomically shaped quad-ring cages and support loops, not triangulated cages. Maintain a broad flattened wedge-shaped snout, strong brow, gill region and continuously tapering muscular torso. Main head/body surface should flow continuously; avoid separate spheres or cylinders for the face. Match the dominant side-view proportions and the frontal mouth shape. The mouth opening is a broad arched upper lip and deep U-shaped lower jaw, NOT a round tube or torus. Build coherent dark interior surfaces behind organized ivory triangular teeth. Eyes are small and far apart on the sides of the head.  Curve and sweep the fin outlines backward with a broad rooted base and thin pointed tips. The pectoral fins extend downward and outward. Tail has a narrow peduncle and crescent lobes. Maintain five curved gill grooves on each side. Conform red flank streaks tightly to the curved skin; no detached slabs, floating ribbons, or arbitrary red rings. The upper skin must be very dark charcoal, the belly pale gray, and the jagged red streaks distinctly visible in side view.  Use all supported material controls. Do not invent unsupported UV/texture fields or claim baked textures. Prioritize actual shape, connected-looking surfaces, coherent color boundaries and silhouette over unsupported texture claims. Subdivision smooths an accurate cage; it does not repair incorrect anatomy. Preserve support loops around mouth, snout, fin roots and thin edges. Respect mesh/part/triangle budgets.  Render and compare the entire silhouette, face, jaw, teeth, fins, tail and color coverage against the actual attached image. Apply visual corrections instead of merely returning a successful file. Name: Hiu Crimson — Rekonstruksi Organik., Placeholder: Jelaskan yang ingin dibuat…
